html:
The Al Sabah are the family that has ruled Kuwait since about the middle of the 1700s, when Sabah I was chosen as its first sheikh.

Kuwait town was founded in the early 1700s by clans of the Bani Utbah who had come from central Arabia. By tradition the families shared out roles: the Al Sabah ran the town and dealt with outsiders, while the merchant families ran trade and pearling. The ruler needed the merchants' money and consent.

That old bargain survived into the oil age. It shows in the constitution of 1962 and the strong elected assembly. Mubarak, who seized power in 1896, put the state under British protection by the agreement of 1899.
sum: The Al Sabah are the family that has ruled Kuwait since about the middle of the 1700s, when Sabah I was chosen as its first sheikh.
